translations.literal: Hunan: the territory of Jing Province in the Yu's Tribute.

sentences.zh: 明屬湖廣布政使司，置偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the Ming it was subordinate to the Huguang Regional Administration Commission, with a Pianyuan grand coordinator established.

translations.literal: The early Qing continued this arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The early Qing kept the same arrangement.

translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664) the Hunan provincial administration commission was split off as Hunan Province, and the Pianyuan grand coordinator relocated to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，改偏沅巡撫為湖南巡撫，並歸湖廣總督兼轄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, the Pianyuan grand coordinator was renamed Hunan grand coordinator and placed under the concurrent jurisdiction of the Huguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 (1724) the post became the Hunan grand coordinator, concurrently overseen by the Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 七年，置永順府，升岳州之澧州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Guiyangzhou in Hengzhou was promoted.

translations.literal: Two garrisons, Zhenxi and Xique—both established in the second year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxi and Xique garrisons were both established in Jiaqing 2 (1797).

translations.literal: Fenghuang Directly Controlled Department: busy, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Fenghuang Direct-Control Department was rated busy and difficult.

sentences.zh: 鎮筸總兵、辰沅永靖道駐。

translations.literal: Zhen'ao regional commander and Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen'ao regional commander and Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit were stationed here.

sentences.zh: 明為五寨、筸子坪二長官司，隸保靖宣慰使司。

translations.literal: Under the Ming it was two native chieftain's offices, Wuzhai and Ganziping, subordinate to Baojing Pacification Superintendent Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming it comprised the native chieftain's offices of Wuzhai and Ganziping, under the Baojing pacification superintendent.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，改流官置通判，辰沅靖道僉事徙駐。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi, converted to regular officials and established subprefectural judge; Chen-Yuan-Jing Circuit vice commissioner relocated station.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 43 (1704) it was placed under regular officials with a subprefectural judge, and the Chen-Yuan-Jing Circuit vice commissioner moved his station here.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng changed to Fenghuang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726) it was renamed Fenghuang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十二年改廳，升通判為同知。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong changed to department, promoted subprefectural judge to associate prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 (1787) it became a department and its subprefectural judge was raised to associate prefect.

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing it was promoted to a directly controlled department.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 (1796) it was raised to a direct-controlled department.

translations.idiomatic: It governed 105 Red Miao stockades.

translations.idiomatic: It lay 1,050 li northeast of the provincial seat.

translations.literal: West: Fenghuang Mountain; atop was Fenghuang Garrison; also Fenghuang Garrison office assistant magistrate for inspections—later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: To the west: Fenghuang Mountain, atop which stood Fenghuang Garrison; it also had a Fenghuang Garrison inspection sub-office, later abolished.

translations.idiomatic: To the southeast: Guanjing.

translations.idiomatic: To the southwest: Dudu.

sentences.zh: 沱江自貴州銅仁入，迤東北流，烏巢江自北來注之。

translations.literal: Tuojiang River entered from Tongren in Guizhou, winding northeast; Wuchao River from the north came to pour into it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuojiang River entered from Tongren in Guizhou and wound northeast, receiving Wuchao River from the north.

sentences.zh: 東過廳治北，又東北入於瀘溪，是為武水最南源也。

translations.literal: East passed north of the department seat, again northeast entered into Luxi—this was the southernmost source of Wu River.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing east past the seat's north side, it continued northeast into Luxi as the southernmost source of Wu River.

sentences.zh: 又，萬溶江源出西北天星砦山，東屈而北，左納龍爪溪，西北至乾州合武水。

translations.literal: Again, Wanrong River source rose northwest at Tianxing Stockade Mountain, east bent north, on the left received Longzhao Stream, northwest to Qianzhou united with Wu River.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong River also rose northwest at Tianxing Stockade Mountain, bent east and north, took Longzhao Stream on the left, and at Qianzhou joined Wu River from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 西南：樂濠溪，東南至麻陽入辰水。

translations.literal: Southwest: Lehao Stream, southeast to Mayang entered Chen River.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest: Lehao Stream flowed southeast to Mayang and entered Chen River.

translations.idiomatic: You Garrison, where the administration secretary was posted.

translations.literal: Desheng Garrison; Wuzhai relay station had patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng Garrison; Wuzhai relay station had a patrol office.

translations.literal: Yongsui Directly Controlled Department: busy, difficult.

translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit.

translations.idiomatic: The Suijing regional commander was stationed here.

sentences.zh: 明，鎮溪千戶所、崇山衛地，隸辰州府瀘溪縣。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, Zhenxi Thousand-Household Office and Chongshan Guard territory, subordinate to Luxi County, Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming it was Zhenxi Thousand-Household Office and Chongshan Guard territory, subordinate to Luxi County in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年置廳吉多營，仍隸辰州府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng established department at Jiduo Garrison, still subordinate to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 (1723) a department was established at Jiduo Garrison, still under Chen Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing it was promoted to a directly controlled department.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 (1796) it was raised to a direct-controlled department.

translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 7 (1802) the seat moved to Huayuan Fort.

translations.idiomatic: It governed 228 Red Miao stockades.

translations.idiomatic: It measured 90 li east to west and 155 li north to south.

translations.idiomatic: To the southwest: La'er.

translations.literal: Niujiao River is the southern source of You River; from Songtao Department in Guizhou it flowed along the border in, north to Chadong city; its left bank was then the border of Youyang Prefecture in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Niujiao River—the southern source of You River—entered along the border from Songtao in Guizhou, north to Chadong city, with Youyang in Sichuan on its left bank.

translations.literal: Bent northeast, bordering Baojing County.
translations.idiomatic: It bent northeast along the border with Baojing County.

sentences.zh: 東過廳治北，臘爾堡河自西南來注之，東北入保靖。

translations.literal: East passed north of the department seat; La'er Fort River from the southwest came to pour into it, northeast entering Baojing.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing east past the seat's north side, it received La'er Fort River from the southwest and entered Baojing to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 西南：高岩河，源出犀牛潭，入乾州為鎮溪，入武水。

translations.literal: Southwest: Gaoyan River, source at Xiniu Pool, entering Qianzhou became Zhenxi, entering Wu River.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest: Gaoyan River rose at Xiniu Pool, became Zhenxi at Qianzhou, and joined Wu River.

sentences.zh: 茶洞，廢知事，隆團、排補二砦廢司。

translations.idiomatic: Chadong had an abolished administration secretary; Longtuan and Paubu stockades had abolished sub-offices.

translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 本芷江晃州堡地，屬沅州府。

translations.literal: Originally territory of Huangzhou Fort in Zhijiang, belonging to Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Huangzhou Fort in Zhijiang, under Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年析置直隸廳，移涼傘通判治焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing partitioned and established directly controlled department, moved Liangsan subprefectural judge administration there.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22 (1817) it was split off as a direct-controlled department and the Liangsan subprefectural judge was relocated there.

sentences.zh: 東北距省治一千二百四十五里。

translations.idiomatic: Wu River lay to the south—also Wushui, also called Yi River.

translations.idiomatic: Its upper course was Zhenyang River, entering from Yuping in Guizhou and joining Longxi to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 過廳治南，左納木多溪，東流會平溪，東北入芷江。

translations.literal: Passed south of the department seat, on the left received Muduo Stream, flowed east united Pingxi, northeast entered Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: It passed south of the seat, took Muduo Stream on the left, flowed east to meet Pingxi, and entered Zhijiang to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 東南：中和溪，一名羅岩江，亦東北流入芷江。
